summary: The note describes the rapid growth of the gig economy and freelance work in the U.S. as of October 2023, with freelancers and gig workers making up nearly 35% of the workforce. It covers the appeal of flexibility alongside the risks of income volatility and missing benefits, the role of digital platforms, corporate adoption, and proposed protections. It projects continued growth, with nearly half of working-age Americans doing independent work by 2025.
one_line: Overview of the growing U.S. gig economy: its benefits, financial risks for freelancers, tech platforms, corporate adoption, legislation, and projected growth.
key_facts: As of September 2023, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reports freelancers and gig workers make up nearly 35% of the U.S. workforce.
Johnathan Andrews, a senior researcher at the McKinley Economic Institute, said the gig economy is reshaping 'the very fabric of our economic system.'
Alicia Martinez, a New York City freelancer, said on September 12, 2023 that finding gigs is not hard, but managing downtime, coverage during dry spells and retirement planning is.
Freelancers often lack health insurance, retirement plans and paid leave that full-time employment can offer.
Michael Johnson, a digital marketing consultant who began freelancing in mid-2023, said being your own boss brings the responsibility of avoiding financial trouble in slower months.
Digital platforms such as Upwork and Freelancer connect freelancers with gigs, and Vivian Lee, a data analyst, says they have democratized finding work but require effective self-marketing.
On October 9, 2023, SynthCorp announced a new division dedicated solely to integrating gig workers into its business model.
SynthCorp CEO Lisa Cheung said embracing the gig economy gives the company agility, innovation and access to top-tier talent.
New York's proposed 'Freelance Isn't Free Act,' slated for discussion in late 2023, aims to ensure freelancers are paid in full and on time.
The Freelancers Union has seen membership swell in recent months and offers resources from contract templates to group health plans.
The Sundial Research Center forecasts that by 2025 nearly half of working-age Americans will have engaged in some form of independent work.
Flexible schedules, remote work and project autonomy appeal especially to Millennials and Gen Zers.
Freelancers are advised to focus on skilling up, networking and financial planning, while companies should develop more collaborative and flexible integration approaches.
